mappings.phasor_function: readbit / readbyte / readchar / readword / readshort / readdword / readint / readfloat  (1071 call sites across the 13 reference scripts)
mappings.kotor_equivalent: Raw typed reads at module_base + RVA, but fed by generated typed views instead of hand-counted offsets
mappings.mechanism: src/image (PE32/ELF32 runtime parse) + src/platform module base. The 'improve on' is generating named views from the corpus ghidra_type table: e.g. CSWSObject.position +0x90, orientation +0x9C, animation +0xD4, current_hp +0xDC, hit_points +0xE0, area_id +0x8C, tag +0x18, plot +0xF8, effects +0x124
mappings.evidence: tmp/mapscratch/check.py walks every Ghidra field_<hex> name and compares to the walked offset. CSWSObject: 77/77 names match, size checksums to 0x228. CSWSCreature: 413/413, 0xac8. CSWParty 47/47, CSWSItem 32/32, CSWSDoor 35/35, CSWSPlaceable 29/29. Independent confirmation of position +0x90: decompiled ExecuteCommandGetPosition (0x0053cae0) reads local_10[0xc].vtable/.id/.object_type off a 12-byte CGameObject and pushes them as x/y/z; element 0xc x 12 = byte 0x90.

mappings.phasor_function: writebit / writebyte / writeword / writeshort / writedword / writeint / writefloat
mappings.mechanism: src/platform page protection (VirtualProtect / mprotect) + src/image. Writes must prefer the engine's own setter where one exists - see the setspeed row for why
mappings.evidence: Infrastructure listed as done in the project brief; offsets validated as above.

mappings.mechanism: struct CExoString (size 0x8): c_string pointer +0x00, length +0x04. Safe read path is routine 168 GetTag or 253 GetName
mappings.evidence: ghidra_type CExoString size 8, both fields named, walk checksums exactly. CSWSObject.tag at +0x18 is a CExoString.

mappings.kotor_equivalent: No widestring in the KOTOR object model; localised text is a TLK strref
mappings.mechanism: routine 239 GetStringByStrRef(int nStrRef); CSWSObject.last_name +0x0C and CSWSCreatureStats.first_name +0x34 are CExoLocString-shaped 8-byte fields, not UTF-16
mappings.evidence: 13 readwidestring call sites in the Phasor corpus have no KOTOR counterpart; the engine stores single-byte CExoString plus a strref index. Mapping is a substitution, not an equivalence.

mappings.kotor_equivalent: KOTOR object id, which also has structure - two allocation ranges, not a flat counter
mappings.mechanism: struct CGameObject: vtable +0x00, id +0x04, object_type +0x08 (size 0xC). Allocation split proven in CGameObjectArray::AddInternalObject 0x004d80e0
mappings.evidence: AddInternalObject: if param_3==0 the id comes from next_object_id_0 (+0x04) and increments; otherwise from next_char_id_0 (+0x0C) and decrements. next_object_id_1 (+0x08) and next_char_id_1 (+0x10) are high-water marks kept by AddExternalObject. So normal objects count up and character objects count down toward each other. A readident equivalent must not assume flatness.

mappings.phasor_function: The base+offset typed-map idiom itself (z4eqrjVN.txt stats_base / ctf_globals / koth_globals blocks)
mappings.kotor_equivalent: Generated typed views, one per engine struct, emitted from the RE corpus
mappings.mechanism: corpus table ghidra_type (1565 types for binary_id=8) -> a generator alongside tools/gen_routine_table.py. Adding a struct becomes a data change, per project rule 2
mappings.evidence: The Phasor scripts hand-maintain comments like 'Confirmed' / 'Guess' next to each offset and disagree with each other. The corpus already carries the layouts with names and a size checksum. Hazard to encode: CSWSItem puts its CSWSObject base at +0x10, not +0x00, so current_hp is +0xDC for creature/door/placeable/trigger and +0xEC for items.

mappings.mechanism: hook app.server_main_loop (CServerExoAppInternal::MainLoop, already required) supplies the `this` receiver; then CServerExoAppInternal::GetGameObject 0x004B1700, or the typed family GetCreatureByGameObjectID 0x004B1790, GetDoorByGameObjectID 0x004B1920, GetPlaceableByGameObjectID 0x004B18D0, GetTriggerByGameObjectID 0x004B1880, GetAreaByGameObjectID 0x004B17E0, GetStoreByGameObjectID 0x004B1AB0, GetWaypointByGameObjectID 0x004B19C0, GetEncounterByGameObjectID 0x004B1A10, GetAreaOfEffectByGameObjectID 0x004B1970, GetSoundObjectByGameObjectID 0x004B1A60. Add as kind="call" sites in data/hooksites.toml
mappings.evidence: data/addresses/k1_steam_103.json resolves app.server_main_loop to 0x004BABB0, exactly the corpus address for CServerExoAppInternal::MainLoop in binary_id=8, so corpus addresses are directly usable for that build. The CServerExoApp-receiver variants (GetGameObject 0x4ae750, GetObjectArray 0x4aed70) are NOT usable alone - they need an AppManager global, and the corpus has no data-symbol table to resolve one from. KOTOR-typed lookup is strictly better than Phasor's untyped getobject.

mappings.mechanism: preferred: routine id 165 EffectMovementSpeedIncrease(int nNewSpeedPercent) / id 451 EffectMovementSpeedDecrease + id 220 ApplyEffectToObject (survives save/load). mappings.kotor_equivalent: Engine-backed globals plus save-hooked script state
mappings.mechanism: routine ids 578/579 GetGlobalBoolean/SetGlobalBoolean, 580/581 GetGlobalNumber/SetGlobalNumber, 194/160 GetGlobalString/SetGlobalString, 692/693 GetGlobalLocation/SetGlobalLocation; per-object 679/680 GetLocalBoolean/SetLocalBoolean, 681/682 GetLocalNumber/SetLocalNumber. Hooks vm.save_script_situation and vm.load_script_situation carry Lua-owned state into the save
mappings.evidence: All ten routine ids verified in k1.json; ExecuteCommandGetGlobalNumber / SetGlobalNumber present in decomp. Both save/load hooks are already declared in data/hooksites.toml with exactly this purpose. Phasor has no save-game concept, so this is strictly additional.

unmappable: gethash(player) - Halo CD-key hash. Single-player KOTOR has no network identity, no account, and no per-player credential. Nothing to map to. 49 call sites in the reference scripts, all for ban lists and admin tables.
getip(player) / getport(player) - no network peer exists. 43 and several call sites respectively, all feeding kick/ban logic.
isadmin(player) / getaccess(player) / the whole privilege tier system - there is one player and they already own the process. A privilege check is meaningless.
votekick / ban / hashban / nameban / ipadminadd / kick / sv_kick - moderation of remote players. No remote players.
svcmdplayer(player, cmd) / privilegedcmd / rcon - executing a server command as or on behalf of another player. Both halves of the concept are absent.
getservername() / changegametype() - no server, and KOTOR has exactly one game mode. GetModuleName (id 561) answers a different question and should not be dressed up as this one.

entervehicle(player, vehicleObjId, seat) / exitvehicle(player) / getplayervehicle(player) - KOTOR has no drivable vehicles and no seat model. The swoop and turret sequences are the SWMG_ subsystem (routine ids 583-688), a separate object model with its own follower/gun-bank/obstacle types; SWMG_GetPlayer (611) and SWMG_GetEnemy (613) do not return CSWSObject-derived objects at all. Presenting SWMG as a vehicle API would mislead.
OnBanCheck(hash, ip) and OnServerCommandAttempt(player, cmd, password) - both are join-time and auth-time hooks on a connection that does not exist.

setnavpoint / the HUD navpoint API - KOTOR's nearest surface is the minimap pin (routine id 386 SetMapPinEnabled), but that toggles an existing designer-placed pin rather than creating a world-space marker, so it is not the same capability.

OnClientUpdate(player, objid) as a per-player position-sync callback - the reference scripts lean on it heavily (it is where the whole z4eqrjVN memory map lives) but it fires from network state replication. The KOTOR replacement is the app.server_main_loop tick, which is a different guarantee: it is not per-player and it is not tied to movement.

OnTeamDecision / OnTeamChange arbitration and team-balance logic - the concept of an auto-balanced team assignment has no KOTOR counterpart. Faction change (id 412) exists, but nothing decides it on the player's behalf.
kotor_only_opportunities: OBJECT_SELF is writable, and that is the single largest capability Phasor has no analogue for. CSWVirtualMachineCommands is 0x10 bytes: vtable +0x00, has_caller_object +0x04, caller_object_id +0x08, commands +0x0C. Verified in the decompiled ExecuteCommandClearAllActions (0x0052f4a0), whose body is literally `if (this->has_caller_object != 0) { id = this->caller_object_id; ... }`. Writing those two fields before dispatch retargets every routine that defaults an argument to OBJECT_SELF and every Action* routine in the table. It is also the generic replacement for routine id 6 AssignCommand, one of only three non-marshallable routines. Independently, the commands table at +0x0C is confirmed by the expected_bytes already committed for vm.execute_command in data/addresses/k1_steam_103.json: 8b54240481fa040300007d178b410c8b decodes to mov edx,[esp+4] / cmp edx,0x304 / jge / mov eax,[ecx+0x0C], and 0x304 equals 772, the exact routine count in data/routines/k1.json.

Dialogue as a scriptable surface. Routine ids 204 ActionStartConversation, 255 BeginConversation, 417 SpeakOneLinerConversation, 701 GetIsConversationActive, 711 GetLastConversation, 238 GetPCSpeaker, 445 GetIsInConversation, 284 SetCustomToken (token substitution into dialogue text), 749 ResetDialogState, 461 SetDialogPlaceableCamera, 505 SetLockOrientationInDialog, 757 CancelPostDialogCharacterSwitch, 205/206 pause and resume. Plus data/events.toml already carries OnDialogConditional, OnCreatureDialogue and OnCreatureEndDialogue on the vm.run_script hook. A Lua runtime that can rewrite a dialogue conditional at runtime is something Halo has no shape for.

Use the routines and treat the struct offset as unverified.

2DA table access, which has NO NWScript routine at all - the entire rules database is invisible to game scripts and would be new capability. C2DA::GetINTEntry 0x413660 `int(C2DA*, int row, CExoString* column, int* out)`, GetFLOATEntry 0x413430, GetCExoStringEntry 0x413270, GetRowIndex 0x4138B0, GetColumnIndex 0x413100, plus C2DA::Load2DArray 0x4144F0-ish and CRes2DA. Typed row structs already exist in the corpus: Appearance2DA (112), Animations2DA (56), AppearanceSounds2DA (24), CreatureSpeed2DA (8, RUNRATE and WALKRATE). Exposing feat, spell, appearance and baseitem tables to Lua is a capability neither Phasor nor NWScript has.

Module transitions and the galaxy map. Routine ids 509 StartNewModule, 242 GetModule, 210 GetModuleFileName, 561 GetModuleName, 198 GetTransitionTarget, 739 ShowGalaxyMap, 740/741 SetPlanetSelectable / GetPlanetSelectable, 742/743 SetPlanetAvailable / GetPlanetAvailable, 744 GetSelectedPlanet, 512 DoSinglePlayerAutoSave, 564 EndGame, 403 ExploreAreaForPlayer, 515 RevealMap. Hook module.load_start (CSWSModule::LoadModuleStart) is already declared as a script reload point, and data/events.toml already carries OnModuleLoad, OnModuleStart, OnModulePlayerEnter and OnAreaTransitionFail. Halo's map cycle is a pale version of this.

The effect system as a first-class Lua type. 87 of the 772 K1 routines return `effect`, applied through id 220 ApplyEffectToObject or id 216 ApplyEffectAtLocation, composed with id 199 EffectLinkEffects, scoped with 112 MagicalEffect / 113 SupernaturalEffect / 114 ExtraordinaryEffect, filtered with 355 VersusAlignmentEffect / 356 VersusRacialTypeEffect / 357 VersusTrapEffect, enumerated with 85 GetFirstEffect / 86 GetNextEffect, inspected with 170 GetEffectType / 89 GetEffectDurationType / 91 GetEffectCreator, removed with 87 RemoveEffect and 710 ClearAllEffects. Verified in decomp: ExecuteCommandEffectDamage builds a CGameEffect, stamps SetCreator from caller_object_id, and returns it through StackPushEngineStructure(VirtualMachine, EFFECT, eff). Phasor has no engine-struct concept whatsoever - its damage API is a float multiplier.

Save and load awareness. Hooks vm.save_script_situation (CVirtualMachineInternal::SaveScriptSituation) and vm.load_script_situation (CVirtualMachine::LoadScriptSituation) are already declared in data/hooksites.toml for persisting Lua-owned state alongside the engine's. Combined with routine id 251 GetLoadFromSaveGame and id 512 DoSinglePlayerAutoSave, a script can survive a save/load round trip. Phasor scripts have no save concept and fall back to writing their own text files.

Stealth XP, a scoring system with no Halo analogue. Routine ids 474 GetCurrentStealthXP, 478 SetCurrentStealthXP, 464 GetMaxStealthXP, 468 SetMaxStealthXP, 480 AwardStealthXP, 481 GetStealthXPEnabled, 482 SetStealthXPEnabled, 498/499 the decrement. Struct side: CSWSCreature.stealth_mode +0x4D1 and detect_mode +0x4D0 (single bytes, both validated by neighbouring field names). Caveat: k1.json records source disagreements at ids 463, 467, 473 and 477, where a secondary enum source names these same StealthXP routines. The disagreement is a systematic off-by-one - in 7 of 8 cases the other source's name lands at exactly id+1 in the chosen table - so the nwscript.nss ids used here are the internally consistent set, but anything cited in the 463-478 band deserves a live check.

Pazaak and the swoop/turret minigames as separately scriptable subsystems. Routine ids 364 PlayPazaak, 365 GetLastPazaakResult; and the whole SWMG_ family, ids 583-688, roughly 100 routines covering follower hit points, gun banks, bullet damage, camera clip planes, player tunnel bounds and obstacle counts. This is effectively a second game inside the game with its own object model, and no Phasor concept touches it.

Typed object lookup, which is better than what Phasor exposes. Phasor's getobject returns an untyped address and every script re-derives the type by reading bytes. KOTOR offers eleven typed lookups off one receiver: GetCreatureByGameObjectID 0x004B1790, GetDoorByGameObjectID 0x004B1920, GetPlaceableByGameObjectID 0x004B18D0, GetTriggerByGameObjectID 0x004B1880, GetAreaByGameObjectID 0x004B17E0, GetStoreByGameObjectID 0x004B1AB0, GetWaypointByGameObjectID 0x004B19C0, GetEncounterByGameObjectID 0x004B1A10, GetAreaOfEffectByGameObjectID 0x004B1970, GetSoundObjectByGameObjectID 0x004B1A60, GetClientObjectByObjectId 0x004B2FD0-region. Exposing these gives Lua a checked cast instead of a guess.

Music, ambience and sound as scriptable state.
